items.title: Letters, sounds and stress
items.blurb: The 24 letters, the letter pairs that make one sound, where the stress falls and the spelling rules that change a word's look but not its sound.

items.title: The article
items.blurb: The definite and indefinite article in every case, the contractions στο/στη/στον, and where Greek uses an article when English does not.

items.title: Masculine nouns
items.blurb: The masculine nouns in -ος, -ας, -ης and -ής/-άς/-ούς/-ές, with their stress shifts, their -δες plurals and their vocatives.

items.title: Feminine nouns
items.blurb: Feminine nouns in -α and -η, the learned type η πόλη / οι πόλεις, feminines in -ος, the -δες plurals of γιαγιά and αλεπού, and the tricky genitive plural.

items.title: Neuter nouns
items.blurb: Neuter nouns in -ο, -ι, -μα, -ος and -ιμο, the odd ones such as το φως and το κρέας, and the loanwords that never change.

items.title: Nouns: special cases
items.blurb: Nouns that are both masculine and feminine, nouns used only in the plural, nouns that change in the plural, surnames and the double forms of everyday words.

items.title: Using the cases
items.blurb: What the nominative, accusative and genitive do: subjects and predicates, objects and prepositions, time phrases, possession, indirect objects, and why "a glass of water" needs no genitive.

items.title: Adjectives and agreement
items.blurb: The adjective types -ος/-η/-ο, -ος/-α/-ο, -ύς/-ιά/-ύ, -ής/-ές and -ης/-α/-ικο, πολύς, colours that never change, and agreement in gender, number and case.

items.title: Comparison: bigger, the biggest, very big
items.blurb: The comparative with πιο and with -ότερος, the irregular forms, "than" with από and παρά, the superlative, the -ότατος form and the everyday intensifiers.

items.title: Adverbs
items.blurb: Adverbs from adjectives in -α and -ως, the everyday adverbs of place, time, frequency and degree, and the pairs that trip learners up: ακόμα and πια, απλά and απλώς, καθόλου.

items.title: Personal pronouns
items.blurb: Strong and weak pronouns, where the weak ones go (before the verb, after an imperative), the order of two pronouns, and the doubling that makes Greek sound natural.

items.el: Κτητικές, δεικτικές, ερωτηματικές και αυτοπαθείς αντωνυμίες
items.title: Possessives, demonstratives, question words and "myself"
items.blurb: δικός μου "mine", αυτός and εκείνος with the article, τέτοιος and τόσος, ποιος, τι and πόσος, ο εαυτός μου, ο ίδιος, μόνος μου and ο ένας τον άλλον.

items.title: Someone, nobody, everything: indefinites and quantifiers
items.blurb: κάποιος and κάτι, κανείς and τίποτα with δεν, κάθε, καθένας, όλος, άλλος, μερικοί, οποιοσδήποτε and οτιδήποτε.

items.title: Numbers, time, dates and money
items.blurb: Cardinal numbers and the ones that agree (1, 3, 4, the hundreds, χίλιοι), ordinals, telling the time, dates and years, prices, ages, halves and percentages.

items.title: Prepositions
items.blurb: σε, από, για, με and the other everyday prepositions, all with the accusative; adverbs that combine with σε and από; and the learned prepositions with the genitive (λόγω, μεταξύ, μέσω).

items.title: How the Greek verb works
items.blurb: Persons and endings, the two stems of every verb (present and aorist), the eight forms built from them, aspect explained with everyday examples, and the principal parts to learn.

items.title: The present tense
items.blurb: The three conjugations (γράφω, αγαπάω, μπορώ), the irregular everyday presents λέω, τρώω, ακούω, πάω, and what the present is used for, including "I've been living here for two years".

items.title: The simple past (aorist)
items.blurb: The past endings and the augment, how to form the aorist stem from the present (-σα, -ψα, -ξα, -ησα, -ασα, -εσα), and when Greek uses the aorist where English says "have done".

items.title: Irregular aorists
items.blurb: The twenty or so everyday verbs whose past you simply learn by heart (είπα, είδα, ήρθα, πήγα, έφαγα, ήπια, πήρα...), with their dependent forms (να πω, να δω, να έρθω) and the idioms built on them.

items.title: The imperfect and aspect in the past
items.blurb: How to form the imperfect (έγραφα, μιλούσα, έλεγα), and how to choose between "I was doing / used to do" and "I did": background, habits, interruptions and polite requests.

items.title: The future: θα and its uses
items.blurb: The two futures (θα γράψω "I'll write" and θα γράφω "I'll be writing"), how to form the dependent stem, the future in time clauses (όταν έρθεις, without θα), and θα for guesses: θα είναι κουρασμένος "he must be tired".

items.title: The subjunctive: να, ας and μη(ν)
items.blurb: Greek has no infinitive: "I want to go" is θέλω να πάω. How να works with both aspects, which verbs take να + present, negating with μη(ν), the free-standing να of wishes and offers, ας "let's", and για να / χωρίς να / αντί να.

items.title: The imperative
items.blurb: Giving orders, instructions and invitations: γράψε / γράψτε, the continuous γράφε, the irregular ones (πες, έλα, φάε, πάρε, κάτσε), pronouns after the verb (δώσ' μου, πες το), and how to soften it all.

items.title: The perfect tenses: έχω γράψει, είχα γράψει, θα έχω γράψει
items.blurb: How to form the perfect, pluperfect and future perfect with έχω + -ει, and when Greek actually uses them: much less than English, which says "I have eaten" where Greek simply says έφαγα.

items.title: Είμαι, έχω, "like" verbs and impersonals
items.blurb: The two most useful verbs and their idioms (έχω δίκιο, έχει κόσμο), "there is" (υπάρχει / έχει), the weather, the reversed verbs αρέσει, λείπει, πονάει, and the impersonals πρέπει, μπορεί, χρειάζεται, αξίζει, φαίνεται, πειράζει, νοιάζει.

items.title: Passive and middle verbs I: present and imperfect
items.blurb: The verbs ending in -μαι: their four present patterns (έρχομαι, θυμάμαι, στενοχωριέμαι, ασχολούμαι), the imperfect in -όμουν, and the four things -μαι can mean: passive, reflexive, reciprocal, or just an ordinary verb (deponent).

items.title: Passive and middle verbs II: aorist, future, imperative, participle
items.blurb: The perfective forms of -μαι verbs: the aorist in -θηκα (κοιμήθηκα, χάρηκα, σηκώθηκα), the dependent in -θώ (θα κοιμηθώ, να βιαστούμε), the imperative in -σου / -θείτε (σήκω, βιάσου, καθίστε), the perfect (έχω κουραστεί) and the participle in -μένος.

items.title: Participles and the gerund
items.blurb: The -οντας / -ώντας form (κάνοντας, μιλώντας) and the rule that it shares the subject of the main verb; -μένος versus -τός adjectives (κλεισμένος / κλειστός, ψημένος / ψητός); the learned participles in -όμενος, -ούμενος and -ων that fill the news and official Greek.

items.title: Negation, questions and particles
items.blurb: Which "not" to use (δεν, μη, όχι), double negatives (δεν είδα τίποτα), ούτε, the question words and tag questions, μήπως and άραγε, and the small particles that give speech its colour: πια, ακόμα, κιόλας, καν, ντε, δα, ρε.

items.el: Συμπληρωματικές προτάσεις: ότι, πως, που, να, αν
items.title: "That", "to" and "whether": ότι, πως, που, να, αν
items.blurb: The four ways to say "that" (ότι, πως, που, να) and when to use each, verbs that change meaning with ότι or να (λέω ότι / λέω να), που after feelings (χαίρομαι που ήρθες), and indirect questions with αν, τι, πού, ποιος.

items.title: Time, cause, purpose, result and concession clauses
items.blurb: Joining ideas like a native speaker: time (όταν, ενώ, μόλις, αφού, πριν, μέχρι να, από τότε που), cause (γιατί, επειδή, αφού, μια και), purpose and result (για να, ώστε, τόσο... που), concession (αν και, παρόλο που, ακόμα κι αν).

items.title: Relative clauses: που, ο οποίος, όποιος, ό,τι
items.blurb: "The man who...", "the house where...", "whoever...": the all-purpose που, the formal ο οποίος (needed after prepositions), "whose", the resumptive pronoun of spoken Greek (η κοπέλα που της μίλησα), and the free relatives όποιος, ό,τι, όπου, όσος.

items.title: Conditionals: αν, άμα, εκτός αν, μακάρι
items.blurb: The three kinds of "if" sentence (real: αν βρέξει, θα μείνουμε; unreal now: αν είχα λεφτά, θα αγόραζα; unreal past: αν το είχα ξέρει, θα σου το είχα πει), colloquial άμα and να, "unless", "in case", and wishes with μακάρι.

items.title: Reported speech
items.blurb: Turning what people said into reported statements (είπε ότι...), questions (ρώτησε αν / πού...) and orders (μου είπε να...), why Greek doesn't need to shift tenses back, how pronouns and time words change, and the reporting verbs that lift your writing: υπόσχομαι, προτείνω, ζητάω, παραδέχομαι, ισχυρίζομαι.

items.title: Word order and emphasis
items.blurb: How free Greek word order really is: the dropped subject, verb-first sentences for news (ήρθε ο Νίκος), topics with a doubling pronoun (τον καφέ τον πίνω σκέτο), contrastive focus, noun-phrase order (το σπίτι το μεγάλο), and cleft sentences (αυτό που θέλω είναι...).

items.title: Word formation: suffixes, prefixes, compounds
items.blurb: How Greek builds words, so one root gives you ten: diminutives (καφεδάκι, γατούλα), verbal nouns (διάβασμα, τρέξιμο, λύση), people, tools and shops (ταξιτζής, ανοιχτήρι, ψαράδικο), adjective endings (σημερινός, ζηλιάρης), prefixes (ξανα-, ξε-, παρα-, κατα-) and compounds (τυρόπιτα, αλατοπίπερο).

items.title: The grammar of spoken Greek
items.blurb: What changes when Greeks talk rather than write: elision (θα 'ρθω, σ' αγαπώ, μου 'πε), the colloquial forms (θες, λένε, ήμουνα, κάνανε), the discourse markers that hold a conversation together (λοιπόν, δηλαδή, βασικά, που λες), and reactions and fragments (Τι λες! Μπα. Καφέ; Σκέτο.).

items.el: Τα ρήματα και τα συμπληρώματά τους
items.title: Verbs and what follows them
items.blurb: Which case or preposition each everyday verb takes (περιμένω τη Μαρία, συμφωνώ μαζί σου, εξαρτάται από σένα), verbs with two objects (σε κερνάω έναν καφέ), the genitive pronoun "for me" and "on me" (μου έκλεψαν το κινητό), linking verbs (γίνομαι, φαίνομαι, θεωρούμαι), the many meanings of παίρνω, περνάω, βγάζω, and verb + noun pairs (κάνω υπομονή, δίνω σημασία).

items.title: Linking ideas: and, but, so, like, the more
items.blurb: The words that join clauses and organise a text: και, ή, είτε... είτε, ούτε... ούτε; αλλά, όμως, ωστόσο, παρ' όλα αυτά; άρα, επομένως, οπότε, επιπλέον, εξάλλου, αφενός... αφετέρου; σαν, όπως, ως, σαν να, λες και; όσο... τόσο and απ' ό,τι; and the signposts of a B2 essay.

items.title: The grammar of written Greek
items.blurb: What changes when Greek is written formally: the internal augment (υπέγραψα, συνέβη, επέστρεψε), learned passives in -ούμαι and -ώμαι (θεωρείται, εξαρτάται), news forms like εξελέγη and ελήφθη, fixed learned phrases (εν λόγω, εκ των υστέρων), turning verbs into nouns (η αύξηση των τιμών), impersonal passives (θεωρείται ότι, αναμένεται να), and switching register (διότι, προκειμένου να, λαμβάνω).

items.title: Spelling, punctuation and abbreviations
items.blurb: How grammar decides spelling (θα λύσει but η λύση, οι καλοί but η καλή), the sound-alikes πως/πώς, που/πού, η/οι/ή, ότι/ό,τι, πια/πιο, the spelling of common endings (-ώνω, -εύω, -ίζω, -ικός, -εια), stress marks on capitals and the diaeresis, Greek punctuation (; · « » —), capital letters, and the abbreviations and number formats of everyday texts.

items.title: Politeness, wishes and exclamations
items.blurb: The grammar of being polite and sociable: εσύ or εσείς, softening a request (θα ήθελα, μήπως θα μπορούσατε), addressing people (κύριε Νίκο, κυρία Παππά, θεία), pet names, the wish for every occasion (Χρόνια πολλά, Περαστικά, Καλορίζικο, Με γεια) and its answer, suggestions and refusals, signs and prohibitions, and exclamations (Τι ωραία που είναι! Πόσο μεγάλωσες! Να τος! Για έλα!).

items.title: Numbers in use: amounts, maths and statistics
items.blurb: Numbers beyond counting: approximate amounts (κάνα δυο, καμιά δεκαριά, γύρω στα σαράντα), groups (δεκάδα, ντουζίνα, εκατοντάδες), double and triple (διπλός, διπλάσιος), fractions and decimals (τα δύο τρίτα, μηδέν κόμμα πέντε), arithmetic (συν, πλην, επί, διά), measurements (τετραγωνικά, βαθμοί), "one in three" and "every other day", and the language of rising and falling figures (αυξήθηκε κατά 5%, έπεσε στο 10%) that the B2 papers use for charts.

items.el: Χρόνος, διάρκεια και φάσεις της πράξης
items.title: Time in use: ago, for, already, nearly, keep doing
items.blurb: The time words English speakers mix up: πριν από / εδώ και / σε / μέσα σε / μέχρι / κατά τη διάρκεια; already, still, yet, just, no longer (ήδη, ακόμα, μόλις, πια); used to, about to and nearly (πήγαινα, ήμουν έτοιμος να, παραλίγο να, κόντεψα να); and the verbs of starting, continuing and stopping (αρχίζω να, συνεχίζω να, σταματάω να, κόβω, όλο, ξανα-).

items.title: Mixed practice in the style of the B2 exam
items.blurb: The language-use tasks of the B2 Certificate in one place, mixing everything in the outline: the right form of a word in brackets (η ολοκλήρωση, αξιοσημείωτος), one missing small word, sentence transformations (active to passive, direct to reported, clause to noun), choosing the right form, and finding the mistake. Many items use words from the app's new 10,000-word list.

items.title: Aspect in practice: choosing the right stem
items.blurb: One decision runs through every Greek verb: the ongoing stem (γράφ-) or the one-off stem (γράψ-). This chapter drills the choice everywhere it appears: after να and θα, past narration (imperfect or aorist), commands and prohibitions, with time words (πάντα, ξαφνικά, για δύο ώρες), and in the minimal pairs where the meaning changes (θα τρώω / θα φάω, μην τρως / μη φας).

items.title: Learned syntax: the formal layer at C1
items.blurb: The older constructions that survive in formal Greek: learned prepositions with other cases (υπό, επί, περί, εκ/εξ, άνευ, μετά + genitive, προ, διά, εν + dative), the many uses of ως (ως εξής, ως γνωστόν, ως επί το πλείστον), formal conjunctions (εφόσον, δεδομένου ότι, μολονότι, ούτως ώστε, καθότι), and the frozen verb forms of official texts (έστω, δέον, ουδείς, ως έχει).
